stories.title: Morganella morganii-derived histamine impairs intestinal barrier function via HRH4 and aggravates colitis
stories.authors_source: Youcai Yi, Rui Feng, Xueting Wu et al. — Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (9 October 2026)
stories.publication_type: Peer-reviewed primary research; advance online publication
stories.takeaway: The authors identify histamine secreted by Morganella morganii as a mediator of intestinal permeability and colitis through histamine receptor H4 (HRH4).
stories.what_happened: M. morganii worsened experimental colitis and impaired epithelial junction architecture. Fractionation and metabolomics implicated a low-molecular-weight secreted product, histamine; histamine exposure reproduced injury, while interventions targeting histamine synthesis or HRH4 improved experimental outcomes.
stories.method: Murine colitis, mouse colonic organoids, intestinal epithelial cells, <3-kDa bacterial supernatant fractionation, metabolomics and pharmacological perturbation.
stories.why_it_matters: A strong public example of moving from microbiome association to a testable microbial-metabolite–host-receptor mechanism using complementary intestinal models.
stories.read_first: Read the supernatant fractionation and histamine-identification results, then HRH4 inhibition and epithelial tight-junction/permeability experiments.
stories.caveat: The mechanistic evidence is primarily from experimental colitis and model systems; therapeutic efficacy and exposure levels in human Crohn's disease remain unestablished.

stories.title: Modulation of dysregulated ATG5 and ATG16L1 expression in IBD by Akkermansia muciniphila and its extracellular vesicles (EVs)
stories.authors_source: Nesa Kazemifard, Maryam Farmani, Kimia Basiji et al. — Scientific Reports (12 October 2026)
stories.takeaway: Live Akkermansia muciniphila and its extracellular vesicles altered inflammation-associated ATG5 and ATG16L1 transcript patterns in an epithelial cell model.
stories.what_happened: Patient-sample qPCR identified differences in ATG5 and ATG16L1 expression in IBD relative to controls. In IL-1β-challenged Caco-2 cells, live bacteria and extracellular vesicles modulated these genes; vesicle responses varied with dose.
stories.method: Patient-derived clinical samples with qPCR, IL-1β-stimulated Caco-2 epithelial cultures, live bacterial and extracellular-vesicle exposures.
stories.why_it_matters: Relevant to microbiome therapeutics and epithelial stress biology because it compares live bacteria with defined bacteria-derived vesicle preparations.
stories.read_first: Start with the patient-sample expression comparison, then the live-bacteria-versus-vesicle dose-response plots for ATG5 and ATG16L1.
stories.caveat: Changes in ATG transcripts do not by themselves establish autophagic flux, epithelial functional rescue or therapeutic efficacy in people.

stories.title: B cells regulate T cell transfer colitis by partially reconstituting luminal IgA and modulating the colonic microbiota
stories.authors_source: Josef Urrete, Margaret Kim, Amruth Chilukuri et al. — Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (12 October 2026)
stories.publication_type: Peer-reviewed primary research; advance online publication
stories.takeaway: Transferred B cells attenuated experimental T-cell-transfer colitis in association with restored secretory IgA and altered microbiota; IgA-deficient B cells did not reproduce the protection.
stories.what_happened: Wild-type B-cell cotransfer partially reconstituted luminal IgA, increased bacterial IgA coating and changed colonic microbial communities while reducing colitis severity. IgA-deficient donor B cells reconstituted peripheral compartments but did not protect comparably.
stories.method: RAG1-deficient mouse T-cell-transfer colitis, wild-type versus IgA-deficient B-cell cotransfer, histology, luminal IgA and microbial community measurements.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides a mechanistic immune–microbiome reference for understanding what additional biology immune-inclusive intestinal models can capture.
stories.read_first: Read the wild-type versus IgA-deficient B-cell transfer comparison, followed by luminal IgA coating and microbiota analyses.
stories.caveat: The lymphopenic adoptive-transfer model isolates a particular immune mechanism and should not be generalized to all IBD contexts or to epithelial-only systems.

stories.title: Hydrogen peroxide sensing and signaling in physiology and disease: implications for therapy
stories.authors_source: Ryan J. Mailloux — Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy (12 October 2026)
stories.takeaway: This review distinguishes damaging oxidant overload from physiological H2O2 signaling and organizes cellular signal transmission into floodgate, redox-relay and S-glutathionylation mechanisms.
stories.what_happened: The author synthesizes evidence that H2O2 acts as a spatially constrained second messenger through reversible protein-thiol chemistry, and considers how signaling distance and cellular antioxidant systems influence outcomes.
stories.method: Mechanistic review of redox biochemistry, H2O2 diffusion/signaling measurements and experimental approaches to thiol oxidation.
stories.why_it_matters: A useful conceptual framework for interpreting oxidant measurements and redox signaling in human-relevant cellular disease models without equating all ROS with damage.
stories.read_first: Read the three-mechanism overview (floodgate, redox relay, S-glutathionylation) and the discussion of H2O2 signaling distance.
stories.caveat: A broad mechanistic synthesis rather than an intestinal-specific experimental study; cellular compartment, oxidant dose and assay chemistry constrain translation.

stories.title: Differential long-term efficacy of biologic and small-molecule therapies by disease location in moderate-to-severe luminal Crohn's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
stories.authors_source: Sóley Poulsen Dalsgarð, Kavini Kalinga Bandara Pkb, Jakob Benedict Seidelin et al. — Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (8 October 2026)
stories.publication_type: Peer-reviewed systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
stories.takeaway: Across 18 randomized trials involving 4,697 patients, relative long-term treatment efficacy varied by Crohn's disease location for some agents, with isolated ileal disease generally showing lower remission rates.
stories.what_happened: The analysis stratified week-52 clinical remission and endoscopic response by ileal, colonic and ileocolonic disease. It reported location-dependent signals for selected treatments rather than a uniform effect across all agents.
stories.method: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials and Bayesian network meta-analysis stratified by Montreal disease location.
stories.why_it_matters: Offers clinical context for why intestinal disease models should specify anatomical region and avoid treating all Crohn's disease presentations as interchangeable.
stories.read_first: Read the disease-location subgroup results and the network-comparison tables, then inspect sensitivity analyses and trial-design stratification.
stories.caveat: Indirect comparisons and sparse location subgroups can destabilize treatment rankings; these estimates are not patient-level treatment rules.

stories.title: A perfusable first-generation endometrial microvascular model to study human spiral artery remodeling in pregnancy
stories.authors_source: Sebastian Naranjo, Madison E. Fletcher, Noo Li Jeon et al. — Lab on a Chip (9 October 2026)
stories.publication_type: Peer-reviewed primary research; advance online publication
stories.takeaway: A modular polystyrene microfluidic system supports perfusable human endometrial microvessels and quantifies hormone- and trophoblast-associated vascular remodeling.
stories.what_happened: Self-assembled human endometrial endothelial cells and fibroblasts formed perfusable networks; hormonal exposures altered vascular features, and two trophoblast cell lines produced different effects on vascular barrier and cell survival.
stories.method: Polystyrene microfluidic NAM, endothelial–fibroblast co-culture, perfusion, trophoblast tri-culture, vascular imaging and permeability/secretome readouts.
stories.why_it_matters: A transferable organ-chip engineering reference for material choice, perfusable multicellular networks, model-specific perturbations and quantitative validation.
stories.read_first: Read the vascular network formation/perfusion figures, then hormone-dependent permeability and trophoblast integration comparisons.
stories.caveat: An early-generation in-vitro model; pregnancy-specific physiology and trophoblast cell lines limit direct extrapolation to clinical outcomes or other organs. Briefing overlap: the 11 October daily brief covered a different placenta-on-chip toxicology study; this article addresses endometrial vascular remodeling instead.

stories.title: Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues
stories.authors_source: Jia Yao, Ji Seon Shim, K. Wong et al. — Nature Biomedical Engineering (13 October 2026)
stories.takeaway: SPACER uses interpretable multi-instance learning to infer gene-level spatial recruitment rules from spatial transcriptomics, with demonstrations across 37 tissue datasets.
stories.what_happened: The framework improved recovery of known recruitment signals in benchmark tasks and associated local antigen presentation and mucin-related tissue features with immune-cell engagement in cancer datasets.
stories.method: Interpretable AI applied to spatially resolved transcriptomics from human tumors and mouse heart, with cross-dataset benchmarking and biological validation analyses.
stories.why_it_matters: Relevant to omics and multicellular tissue modeling as a way to generate hypotheses about spatial cell organization rather than relying on cell-type abundance alone.
stories.read_first: Read Fig. 1 for model logic, then the T-cell recruitment and antigen-presentation benchmark figures.
stories.caveat: Inferred recruitment rules are not proof of causality, and the published applications are not intestinal disease models. Briefing overlap: the 9 October daily brief discussed a disease tissue atlas and cell-communication inference; SPACER is a distinct spatial-recruitment method.

stories.title: Gut guardians: the enteric neuroimmune-microbiota axis in health and disease
stories.authors_source: Ziwen Ma, Mengyan Dang, Wanting Hou et al. — Journal of Neuroinflammation (12 October 2026)
stories.takeaway: The review organizes bidirectional signaling among enteric neurons/glia, mucosal immune cells and microbial metabolites across intestinal physiology and disease.
stories.what_happened: It surveys neuroimmune interactions, microbial signals including short-chain fatty acids and tryptophan derivatives, and proposed roles in IBD, enteritis, Hirschsprung's disease and colorectal cancer.
stories.method: Narrative mechanistic review of enteric nervous system biology, immune-cell interactions, microbiota signaling and experimental technologies.
stories.why_it_matters: Broadens the conceptual scope of intestinal model design to include neural and immune compartments in addition to epithelial and microbial components.
stories.read_first: Read the diagrams of neuroimmune–microbiota signaling and the IBD-specific section, followed by emerging experimental technologies.
stories.caveat: Integrates heterogeneous experimental systems and disease contexts; not every proposed circuit is causally established in humans.

stories.title: Spatial confinement enables reproducible engineering of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms by 3D bioprinting
stories.authors_source: E. Roscetto, G. Balato, M. Aversa et al. — Scientific Reports (9 October 2026)
stories.takeaway: An alginate '3D-Sandwich' that spatially confines bacteria produced more rapid and organized biofilms than a homogeneously mixed 3D construct.
stories.what_happened: At 48 hours the confined construct achieved culturable counts comparable to a mixed construct at 96 hours; confocal and electron microscopy, nearest-neighbor analysis and Raman spectroscopy documented structural and biochemical differences.
stories.method: 3D bioprinted alginate biofilm geometries versus 2D controls, bacterial counts, CLSM, SEM, spatial analysis and Raman spectroscopy.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how initial microbial spatial architecture can change culture behavior and reproducibility, a general consideration in engineered host–microbe platforms.
stories.read_first: Read the 3D-Sandwich versus 3D-Mixed time-course comparisons and the microscopy/nearest-neighbor analyses.
stories.caveat: A single-species Staphylococcus infection/biofilm model, not a gut microbial consortium or host epithelial co-culture.

stories.title: Engineering biocomputability in living and material systems
stories.authors_source: Ryan Gharios, Murial L. Ross, Annabella Li et al. — Nature Chemical Engineering (12 October 2026)
stories.takeaway: The review compares nucleic-acid, protein and synthetic-material logic circuits that enable living cells and biomaterials to sense and respond to combinations of inputs.
stories.what_happened: The authors categorize biocomputation strategies and survey programmable cell and material systems, including stimuli-responsive approaches relevant to tissue engineering.
stories.method: Cross-disciplinary review of synthetic biology, logic-gated biological circuits and responsive biomaterial design.
stories.why_it_matters: A forward-looking engineering reference for responsive tissue platforms, multiplex sensing and the distinction between passive measurements and programmable biological responses.
stories.read_first: Start with the circuit taxonomy and Figs. 2–6 comparing nucleic-acid, protein and material-based logic systems.
stories.caveat: Conceptual breadth is stronger than direct organ-chip validation; integration complexity, robustness and long-term biocompatibility require system-specific tests.
